observation.visible_scene: A fixed wide shot of a small bonfire burning on a sandy beach at sunset. Two dark logs/branches form a V-shape at the fire (one angled up-left, one lying to the right). Behind them is a calm sea with a flat horizon, and a sky grading from teal-blue (upper left) to orange-red (right and along the horizon). The firelight casts a persistent red glow on the foreground sand.
visible_changes: The flame continuously flickers and deforms: its height, brightness and outline change from frame to frame while its base stays fixed at the same spot on the logs.
Around t=0.32–0.56 s the upper part of the flame forms a distinct pale curling, smoke-like loop above the brighter orange base; this loop then shifts and thins.
In the later frames (t≈1.28–1.60 s) the flame becomes taller and thinner, and small bright particles (embers/sparks) appear above it and drift upward (most visible at t=1.52–1.60 s).
The red illumination on the sand and the flame's overall brightness pulse subtly in sync with the flickering.
The logs, horizon, sea line and cloud shapes hold constant positions across the segment, indicating no camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fire was already burning at the start and continues past the end of the excerpt; its ignition, fuel, and later outcome are not shown.
No people, wind source, or other actors are visible within the segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the curling flame shape reflects a light breeze is not directly observable.
The rising bright dots could be embers or illuminated smoke; their exact nature is uncertain.
Any motion of the sea surface is too subtle to confirm from these frames.
